title: Solo Results Playbook — personal KPI scratchpad
content:
Purpose
- Lightweight, personal playbook to turn high-level OKRs into weekly habits and measurable outputs. Not a manager doc — for my own cadence.

North-star (one line)
- Decrease mean end-to-end response tail (p95 latency) for demo flows by 20% while keeping cost per 1k tokens +/-5%.

Quarterly objectives (first draft)
O1: Improve demo reliability and latency for high-traffic flows
  KR1.1: p95 latency reduced from 420ms -> 340ms for demo-v2 (avg of sample week)
  KR1.2: Incidents impacting demo flows <= 1 per month (sustained)
  KR1.3: Add automated smoke checks covering 90% of demo routes
O2: Make serving configurations repeatable + lower unit cost
  KR2.1: Identify 3 model/quantization combo wins that lower token cost by 12% in lab workloads
  KR2.2: Create a config template repo and land 2 production rollouts from it
O3: Personal growth — ship faster, fewer WIP forks
  KR3.1: Cut average PR review turnaround from 48h -> 24h
  KR3.2: Run 4 focused postmortems/learning notes (private)

Notes on KRs — raw thoughts
- Demo-v2 p95 is noisy: need consistent bench harness; sample size = 2000 requests over 3 days to validate any change.
- Smoke checks = small end-to-end traces that assert KV cache warm path; can reuse smoke harness from platform-e2e.
- Quantization experiments: start with 4-bit/8-bit baseline on small corpus. Aim to measure output quality drift via eval set (BLEU-ish sim, not perfect).

Weekly check-in template (quick log)
- Week range: 2026-03-02 — 2026-03-08
- Focus priorities (top 3): 1) bench harness for p95 sampling; 2) PR: config templates; 3) schedule micro-retro with SRE
- Wins: prototyped smoke check script (covers 11 routes); trimmed non-critical logging in demo service (saved ~8% CPU on host)
- Blockers: need access to dedicated test pool to reproduce p95 tail reliably; infra request stuck (PROD-1123).
- Owner actions this week: 1) push follow-up in PROD-1123; 2) split bench into two jobs (short/long) and run night batch; 3) pair with Jordan on rollout checklist
- Metrics snapshot: p95 (sample) = 412ms, cost/1k tokens = $0.79
- Quick retrospective: small wins feel sticky; logging change low risk, but need better gating for smoke checks.

Habit experiments (2-week runs)
- Experiment A: 'Focus hour' 9–10am every day to triage alerts + quick dev tasks. Hypothesis: dedicated slot reduces context switching and PR churn.
  Measurement: number of context-swaps (est via time-block logging), PR cycles closed.
- Experiment B: 'Micro-ship Fridays' — every Friday send one small deliverable (doc/PR/metric). Hypothesis: increases cadence and reduces WIP.
  Measurement: #deliverables/month.

Retro prompt bank (short)
- What small change removed the most friction this week?
- Where did I over-commit? Why?
- What signal would I like more of next week? (latency histograms, error tags)
- One lesson to write down and close the loop on.

Action item backlog (priority order)
- A1: Follow up on infra ticket PROD-1123 (request dedicated test pool) — blocker for bench runs. Next step: DM infra lead + escalate if no response by Wed.
- A2: Draft and land config-template README + example for demo-v2. Target PR: end of week.
- A3: Small smoke-check CI job: create job YAML and add to repo. Low risk.
- A4: Schedule 30m pairing session with Jordan to align rollout checklist.
- A5: Create a 45-min learning note for last incident (template in Confluence), add to KR3.2 list.

Loose ideas (brain dump)
- Could we use a persistent prefix cache in dev harness to simulate warm tail? Might reduce noise.
- Thought: maintain a 'ship ledger' — list of micro-deliverables with tags (doc, infra, perf) and quick notes on impact.
- If quantization shows <3% quality drift, slot it into a canary rollout path.

Open questions
- How to standardize p95 sampling window across teams? Proposal: 3-day rolling sample with 2k requests.
- What cost-accounting delta is acceptable for a latency win? (I said +/-5% but need stakeholder buy-in)

Quick links and reminders
- Related ticket: PROD-1123 (bench infra request)
- Bench harness: github.com/redwood/bench-harness (local folder: /bench/demo)
- Slack tags: #infra-help, #demo-observability

Final quick note to self
- Keep this as a short, living log: move finished items to a monthly "ship ledger" doc. Avoid over-structuring — the value is in speed and reflection.

---
History (short)
- 2026-02-15: created initial template and populated Q1 objectives
- 2026-02-22: added habit experiments and weekly check-in scaffold
- 2026-03-07: updated with current week snapshot and actions
